title: Heat Pump Rebates in Kingston 2026: Owners, Landlords and Renters
desc: Kingston heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings, where 44% of households rent: only owners can apply, and the rate depends on your current heating fuel.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Kingston has 57,835 households, 44% of them renters. The heat pump rebate is for owners only, which shapes how landlords and tenants should approach it.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Kingston
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 56% of Kingston households owning and 44% renting. 63% live in an eligible house type. 17% live in tall apartments, 16% in low-rise apartments and 2,190 in duplexes. The applicant must own the home and pay for the installation, and a tenant cannot apply for the owner.

The requirements document allows an individual unit in a stacked townhome, duplex or triplex to apply if the applicant applies only for that unit and the unit has its own independent heating system and meter. The program's web page lists only houses, semis, rows, townhomes and mobile homes, so confirm with the program if you own such a unit.

A rented heat pump pays $500 per ton up to $2,000 for any heating fuel, and a ground-source rental pays $3,000 flat. A Kingston owner who does not want the upfront cost could consider this route, but compare the rental total over its term with buying.

53% of households live in homes built before 1981, and 6.5% report needing major repairs. Older masonry houses may have little space for ducts, which pushes some owners toward ductless systems. The program accepts ductless and multi-head systems if the whole conditioned space can be heated.

The pre-installation application needs a fully itemized work order, photos of the existing heating system and nameplates, the signed participant agreement and the NRCan sizing form for each outdoor unit. Kingston owners of older houses should have the nameplates accessible before the visit, because approval depends on them.
claim_steps: Confirm that you own the home or the unit and that it has its own heating system and meter.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
faq: Can a unit in a duplex apply?
The requirements allow it with independent heating and a meter, but confirm with the program.
